title: Element hunt sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 25 (Element hunt sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 25: Dalton's atoms and elements. To understand how Dalton's atomic model explains elements and compounds

questions.q: Is CO₂ an element or a compound? Explain.
questions.a: A compound: it has carbon and oxygen atoms chemically joined
questions.model: Count the types of atom: C and O, two types. Are they joined? Yes, in one molecule. So it is a compound.

questions.q: How many atoms in one H₂O molecule?
Element hunt at home: list five household items and the elements they contain (labels, packets, an adult can help). Use a periodic table.
questions.a: For example: foil: aluminium (Al); salt: sodium and chlorine (Na, Cl); water: H and O; pencil lead: carbon (C); copper pipe: Cu
questions.model: Teacher does the first: kitchen foil, aluminium, Al.

questions.q: Which of Dalton's ideas do we now know are not quite right? Explain one.
questions.a: Atoms can be split; atoms of one element are not all identical (isotopes).

questions.q: Why did scientists keep Dalton's model even though parts were wrong?
questions.a: It explained many observations (fixed ratios in compounds) and was improved rather than thrown away.

questions.q: Big question: what do gold, oxygen and carbon have in common?
questions.a: All are elements, made of their own type of atom.
